A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same MedSegFactory work, with readable text, equations, six tables and eight figures. All 12 pages of v1 and 11 pages of v2 were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4.3–4.5 report original image-generation, downstream segmentation and JCA ablation results in Tables 2–6 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: Sections 4.3–4.5 retain the original generation, segmentation and ablation experiments, with small numerical revisions in Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same dual-stream diffusion architecture, Joint Cross-Attention, text conditioning and training objective. No algorithmic component or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use AMOS, ACDC, BUSI, CVC-ClinicDB, Kvasir-SEG, KiTS19 and LiTS17. CT, MRI, ultrasound and colonoscopy generation and segmentation coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 2–5 is unchanged: generation uses SDM, fine-tuned SDM, ControlNet, DiffBoost and MAISI where applicable; segmentation retains the same nnUNet control and augmentation comparisons.

E3.justification: Table 1 split sizes and Sections 4.2–4.4 settings remain identical, including 300 training epochs, generation resolution, 50 denoising steps, evaluation metrics and held-out segmentation testing.

E4.justification: The JCA-removal and directional-branch ablations, alignment and diversity examples, and target-free failure cases are retained. Table 6 changes one aggregate score, without changing the ablation configurations or analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The practice of averaging ablation metrics across datasets is unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 5 changes MedSegFactory's AMOS DSC from 76.79% to 76.76% and IoU from 70.42% to 70.48%. Table 6 correspondingly changes the full-model average IoU from 71.26% to 71.27%. Other scores, comparative rankings and qualitative findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The task definitions, diffusion formulation, attention equations and loss in Equations 1–6 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about text-guided paired generation, JCA alignment and synthetic-data benefits for downstream segmentation.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and Section 4.6 limitations are unchanged, including blurred boundaries without segmentation targets and the 2D architecture's limited ability to capture 3D spatial relationships.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 retains the same implementation disclosures, including AdamW, learning rate 1e-5, batch size 20, four A6000 GPUs and guidance scale 7.5. The project link and other reproducibility information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning and all 72 cited works are retained. Changed citation back-reference page numbers reflect layout changes.

P1.justification: The arXiv header changes from v1 dated 9 April 2025 to v2 dated 11 July 2025. Substantive prose, terminology and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Spacing around figures, captions and tables is tightened. Table 4 moves from page 8 to page 7, and the conclusion moves from page 9 to page 8. Figure content, table structures, captions and best-score highlighting remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The three small numerical updates in Tables 5–6 preserve rankings and conclusions, while layout adjustments retain the same content and legibility. Scientific support, explanations, limitations and reproducibility remain unchanged, yielding no meaningful net difference in overall quality.
